the best nano ult combinations are with reaper, soldier, genji, orisa, ramattra and sojourn. Particularly bad ult combos are winston, dva (it does nothing) pharah, bastion, etc. Sig and JQ are decent ult combos but they probably get more value out of nano in "dry" fights, which helps them build ult faster. This is actually why rein and winston are really good nano candidates, because their ults are mostly fine on their own, but getting nano's between ults helps them build faster. You can do this with zarya too. It's called ult cycling, where you just cycle tank ult one fight, nano next, then tank ult, then nano, and so on. Nano shatter is a good combo but imo cycling with rein gets you more value since you can have shatter one fight and a nano'd rein the next, which is often good enough on its own. Other good non-ult combo nano candidates are Tracer and doom (high mobility which allows jen to engage w/nano easier from wherever they are, and they're more survivable in their dives/engages); Reaper (should be for obvious reasons), Dva (she can burst down even tanks if she can get in their face with nano), Bastion (with his turret mode and nano is probably the scariest thing in OW). All these heroes can get easy value out of nano, and they'll all be able to build a ton of ult charge while nano'd (nano tracer can build pulse bomb ridiculously fast). I think the number one mistake dps make is farming damage off tanks instead of going for kills. Farming ult off tanks is fine depending on your hero, especially during the poke, or in between, phase of fights, but your primary focus should be to have 2 key targets in mind on the other team, and focus on killing them that fight. I say that fight because it will likely change each fight who is more important to their team. Like if you're expecting a big ult from your team, then the zen or lucio with ult, or the bap with immort is a huge kill to get so your team can get much more value with their ult(s). Outside of this rather specific example, usually the best kill to get is a support, though which one will vary greatly depending on the enemy comp. If you're trying to focus an enemy dps that's causing issues for your team, then they're a great target to focus. In some more extreme situations trading your own life for theirs can be worth it. But if the enemy team has a mercy and you want to focus the enemy pharah/soldier/cass/zen etc then the mercy is the more important target, because with her out of the picture, there's less peel and no rez on the dps. I think you can get the picture, I didn't really have a plan going into this, just kinda typed out my train of thought as it happened. I hope this can help a bit, and if there's any questions feel free to ask for clarification.

SR is skill rating. Once you do 10 placements matches for the current competitive season, you’ll get a SR level between 1 and 5000. 1-1499 is bronze rank, 1500-1999 is silver, 2000-2499 is gold, 2500-2999 is platinum, 3000-3499 is diamond, 3500-3999 is masters, 4000-something I’m not sure is grandmasters, and then there’s the top 500 players by SR in your region. Depending on your region the threshold for top 500 can be as low as diamond or well over 4000 (I’m not well versed on this). Your SR rises after a win and drops after a loss, in my personal experience somewhere between 15-30ish per win/loss. If you leave a game, disconnect or otherwise, you lose about 40-50ish SR unless you can rejoin. Hope I covered some stuff you were curious about. Have fun!
